ambiguities.impact: Positivity of epsilon is inherited from the paper's threshold convention rather than independently quantified in the lemma.
ambiguities.issue: Lemma 3.1 explicitly requires beta > 0 but does not restate epsilon > 0.

ambiguities.evidence: PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, anchor: conditional clause preceding (3.1), followed by the replacement of A_tilde with A + E in the proof.
ambiguities.impact: The literal computation uses A_tilde = X Y^T; its interpretation as a computation of Av is justified only through the backward perturbation in (3.2).
ambiguities.issue: The phrase "the matrix-vector product Av is computed as X(Y^T v)" conflates the target product with evaluation using its approximation.

ambiguities.evidence: PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, anchor: second line of equation (3.2); the exact preceding line exposes epsilon gamma_c beta.

contract_plain_english: Given a b-by-b real matrix A, a factorized low-rank approximation A_tilde = X Y^T with orthonormal columns in X and Frobenius error at most epsilon beta, evaluating X(Y^T v) in floating-point arithmetic produces a result that is exactly (A + Delta A)v for a normwise matrix perturbation bounded by gamma_c||A|| + epsilon(1 + gamma_c)beta, where c = b + r^(3/2); the mixed epsilon gamma_c beta term is only later abbreviated as O(u epsilon) (PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, anchor: Lemma 3.1 and equation (3.2)).

source_evidence.anchor: Lemma 3.1, equations (3.1)-(3.4), and the final sentence of the proof
source_evidence.observation: Lemma 3.1 specifies the dimensions, low-rank factorization, orthonormality and approximation hypotheses, the evaluation order X(Y^T v), the backward-error bounds relative to both A_tilde and A, and the replacement A_tilde = A + E with ||E|| <= epsilon beta.

source_evidence.anchor: paragraph beginning "Note that for the particular choice beta = ||A||"
source_evidence.observation: The paper specializes (3.2) to beta = ||A|| and states the resulting normwise forward-error bound.

source_evidence.anchor: paragraph beginning "Throughout this article the unsubscripted norm"
source_evidence.observation: Unsubscripted norms are Frobenius norms, which are submultiplicative and invariant under left multiplication by a matrix with orthonormal columns.

source_evidence.anchor: equation (2.5) and the definition of gamma_k
source_evidence.observation: The analysis uses fl(x op y) = (x op y)(1 + delta), |delta| <= u, and gamma_k = ku/(1-ku) for ku < 1; noninteger gamma indices are permitted.

source_evidence.anchor: Assumption 2.1 and the paragraph following it
source_evidence.observation: The paper ignores rounding errors in truncated-SVD compression and assumes throughout the analysis that unit roundoff u is safely smaller than the low-rank threshold epsilon.

source_evidence.anchor: paragraph beginning "The bounds (3.1) and (3.5) generalize" and paragraph beginning "It is important to note"
source_evidence.observation: The epsilon term is identified with low-rank truncation, gamma_c with floating-point error, and epsilon gamma_c with their mixed accumulation; the results are explicitly normwise rather than componentwise.

statement.algorithm_linkage: The claim applies specifically to computing the approximate matrix-vector action through the low-rank factors as X(Y^T v); it is not a claim about directly multiplying the full matrix A by v or about the opposite parenthesization (PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, anchor: algorithm clause in Lemma 3.1).
binders: A is in R^(b x b), X and Y are in R^(b x r), and v is in R^b (PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, anchor: opening sentence of Lemma 3.1).

A_tilde = X Y^T is the low-rank approximation, beta is a positive scalar, epsilon is the low-rank threshold inherited from Section 2, and zhat denotes the floating-point result (PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, anchor: Lemma 3.1; PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, anchor: definition of epsilon in (2.4)).
conclusions: There is a perturbation Delta A_tilde such that zhat = (A_tilde + Delta A_tilde)v and ||Delta A_tilde|| <= gamma_c ||A_tilde||, where c = b + r^(3/2) (PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, anchor: equation (3.1) and the following definition of c).
There is a perturbation Delta A such that zhat = (A + Delta A)v and ||Delta A|| <= gamma_c ||A|| + epsilon(1 + gamma_c) beta (PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, anchor: equation (3.2)).

The second bound is also written as ||Delta A|| <= gamma_c ||A|| + epsilon beta + O(u epsilon); this rewriting retains the mixed epsilon gamma_c beta contribution inside O(u epsilon) (PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, anchor: second line of equation (3.2)).

For the particular choice beta = ||A||, the paper explicitly specializes the bound to ||Delta A|| <= (epsilon + gamma_c + epsilon gamma_c)||A|| and derives ||zhat - Av|| <= (epsilon + gamma_c + epsilon gamma_c)||A|| ||v|| (PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, anchor: paragraph immediately following the proof of Lemma 3.1).
constants_and_indexing: The error constant is c = b + r^(3/2), not b + r, b + r^2, or a block-count parameter (PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, anchor: line immediately following equation (3.1)).
gamma_c is a single gamma quantity indexed by c; it is not c times gamma or gamma raised to a power (PDF pp. 4 and 6, printed pp. 954 and 956, anchors: definition of gamma_k and equation (3.1)).
definitions_and_conventions: Writing A_tilde = A + E with ||E|| <= epsilon beta, the final perturbation can be understood as E plus the floating-point perturbation from (3.1); the triangle inequality and ||A_tilde|| <= ||A|| + epsilon beta give (3.2) (PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, anchor: final sentence of the proof).

All unsubscripted matrix and vector norms in the lemma are Frobenius norms; for vectors this agrees with the Euclidean norm (PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, anchor: definition of the unsubscripted Frobenius norm).
The proof forms what = fl(Y^T v) and then zhat = fl(X what), rather than forming A_tilde explicitly (PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, anchor: equations (3.3) and (3.4)).
error_notions: Equation (3.1) is a normwise backward error relative to the low-rank matrix A_tilde (PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, anchor: equation (3.1)).

Equation (3.2) is a combined normwise backward error relative to the original matrix A, incorporating both low-rank truncation and floating-point errors (PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, anchor: equation (3.2) and final proof sentence).

The subsequent forward-error inequality follows from the backward relation and submultiplicativity; it is not an independent componentwise guarantee (PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, anchor: paragraph after the proof; PDF p. 7, printed p. 957, anchor: normwise-only discussion).
exceptional_values: The gamma definition requires c u < 1 (PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, anchor: gamma_k = ku/(1-ku) for ku < 1).

Lemma 3.1 states no separate overflow, underflow, NaN or infinity hypothesis; those cases are outside the elementary relative-error model (PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, anchor: equation (2.5); PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, anchor: Lemma 3.1).
higher_order_terms: The exact stated combined bound contains epsilon gamma_c beta through epsilon(1 + gamma_c) beta; the paper then denotes this mixed contribution by O(u epsilon) (PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, anchor: the two lines of equation (3.2)).

The O(u epsilon) notation does not license dropping the explicit epsilon beta truncation term or the gamma_c ||A|| floating-point term (PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, anchor: equation (3.2); PDF p. 7, printed p. 957, anchor: three-term interpretation).
hypotheses: X has orthonormal columns, equivalently X^T X = I in the paper's convention (PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, anchor: hypotheses of Lemma 3.1; PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, anchor: discussion of orthonormal columns).
The approximation satisfies ||A - A_tilde|| <= epsilon beta for some beta > 0 (PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, anchor: hypotheses of Lemma 3.1).

The multiplication is evaluated in the specific order z = X(Y^T v), first forming Y^T v and then multiplying by X (PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, anchor: conditional clause immediately before equation (3.1)).
implicit_context: The paper's standing analysis assumes u is safely smaller than epsilon and treats truncated-SVD compression as satisfying the prescribed approximation bound without additional SVD-rounding error; Lemma 3.1 itself directly assumes the approximation inequality (PDF p. 5, printed p. 955, anchor: Assumption 2.1 and following paragraph; PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, anchor: Lemma 3.1 hypotheses).
The result is normwise only; no componentwise backward-error claim is made (PDF p. 7, printed p. 957, anchor: paragraph beginning "It is important to note that Lemma 3.1").
norms: Every displayed error bound uses the Frobenius norm, including ||A||, ||A_tilde|| and the perturbation norms (PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, anchor: convention for unsubscripted norms).

The proof uses Frobenius-norm invariance under left multiplication by X with orthonormal columns to identify ||Y|| with ||A_tilde||, and uses ||X|| = sqrt(r) (PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, anchor: equations (3.3)-(3.4) and their explanatory text).
numerical_model: Each elementary operation obeys fl(x op y) = (x op y)(1 + delta), |delta| <= u, for op in {+, -, multiplication, division} (PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, anchor: equation (2.5)).

gamma_k means ku/(1-ku), defined when ku < 1; therefore gamma_c requires c u < 1, and the paper permits noninteger indices such as c = b + r^(3/2) (PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, anchor: definition of gamma_k and the sentence allowing noninteger j and k).

The proof bounds the first multiplication with gamma_b and the second with gamma_r, then combines them into gamma_c (PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, anchor: equations (3.3)-(3.4) and the following combination).

undebatable_constraints: The dimensions are A in R^(b x b), X,Y in R^(b x r), and v in R^b (PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, anchor: Lemma 3.1 opening sentence).
X must have orthonormal columns and A_tilde must equal X Y^T (PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, anchor: Lemma 3.1 hypotheses).
The low-rank approximation condition is normwise: ||A - A_tilde|| <= epsilon beta with beta > 0 (PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, anchor: Lemma 3.1 hypotheses).
The evaluation order is X(Y^T v) (PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, anchor: computation clause before (3.1)).
Both backward-error conclusions, relative first to A_tilde and then to A, must be preserved (PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, anchors: equations (3.1) and (3.2)).
The exact combined bound must retain epsilon(1 + gamma_c) beta, including its mixed epsilon gamma_c beta part (PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, anchor: first line of equation (3.2)).
The constant is c = b + r^(3/2), and all norms are Frobenius norms (PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, anchor: definition of c; PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, anchor: norm convention).
